doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Playing in Atlantic City at fifteen and hearing the jazz greats
summary: At 15 he took a summer job at Eddie's Shamrock in Atlantic City and heard jazz greats, including Ray Charles.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well when I went to high school I couldn’t play accordion in band or orchestra so I started to play bass. And between playing bass and also playing accordion, it was an interesting start. At the age of 15, now this you’ll get a kick out of – at the age of 15 there was a place in Atlantic City that the older musicians were playing in. The kids were like 17, 18 years old. And they got another job in another place and they needed a band to go to Eddie’s Shamrock, which is on Kentucky Avenue. I was 15 going on 16, I got an ABC card, spent the summer in Atlantic City for 60 bucks a week, seven nights a week and two matinees. But here’s what was cool: up the street was the Harlem Club, and also the jazz musicians in that area – I got a chance to see most of the jazz greats that came in, 15, 16 years old. I heard Ray Charles sing “Hallelujah” before the record came out. And so --
All that like gets inside you I think, and later on you may not even remember where it came from but you use it.
